items.text: A stranger faces serious harm. You could prevent it at modest cost to yourself. Assume helping would not advance your own long-term good. What moral weight does the stranger's need have?

options.label: Their need gives me a duty to help.
Their need gives me a moral reason to help, but no duty.
Their need alone gives me no moral reason to help; only my own long-term good can do that.
I am unsure whether their need gives me a moral reason to help.

items.notes: Authored contrast between an independent duty, an independent but non-obligatory moral reason, and an exclusively self-interested moral reason. The first two options oppose only the narrow exclusive moral-end proposition; own_good_only supports it. Undecided is non-directional. This hypothetical has not undergone philosophical, comprehension, localization, or empirical review and cannot alone establish the standard maximizing account of ethical egoism.
